items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: That goes for General Eisenhower down to the Corporal.

ctx.x: It was just perfect. But then that was broken up. You know, the Army does a lot of things with no explanation, because there are so many people in the Army who are getting paid, and they have to think up things to do to earn the money. That goes for General Eisenhower down to the Corporal. See, that's why they call the Private a Buck Private, because he has nobody to pass the buck to. So anyway, we were shipped out and we were shipped to Camp Breckenridge, Kentucky, and the same thing down there, we were in this…

We didn't have to do, you know, any soldiering, in a way of speaking. And this was an infantry regiment, infantry. We who were in the band didn't have anything to do, but it was an unauthorized band, by grace of the Colonel, and we had our own barrack and which was just the Colonel's doing, because the 372nd Infantry was a Boston regiment, was an old National Guard regiment which had battle flags from World War I and the Spanish-American War. And it -- and it was a funny thing, not funny, but the thing was on the…
